observation.evaluation:
Correctness: PARTIALLY_CORRECT  
Safety: CAUTION  
Issues: Single lateral radiograph with an “L” marker at the top right cannot reliably lateralize a pleural effusion; the L marker indicates projection/side closest to the detector, not that the effusion is left; posterior costophrenic angle blunting is visible but nonspecific and may reflect either hemithorax, pleural thickening, atelectasis, or effusion; no frontal PA/AP or prior imaging confirms left-sided localization.  
Suggestion: Review a frontal PA/AP radiograph or prior/CT imaging to confirm laterality before accepting “left pleural effusion”; if only this lateral view is available, report the effusion as side-indeterminate rather than left.
